comparator.sourceNotes: Adopted ESSB 2026–2027 EER Appendix III C p.39 and current public programme overview independently checked 20 October 2026: 23 components, three 60-EC years, compulsory 6.5-EC Designing Social Research, 7.5-EC year-2 Research Project, 15-EC year-3 minor and compulsory 15-EC Bachelor Project. Contrary to the earlier checkpoint, the current public overview now also lists Designing Social Research. Open minor space is preserved without inventing its content; approved exchange/internship possibilities remain choices, not additional credits. This v2 decision is a guarded recovery of an existing record whose earlier root decision was absent, not a replay of a historical decision. Enriched workbook blob c2bcc3b63ec7831fd0f7b8ddfb32de1260521655 supplies current course content, prerequisites and availability.

questionsApplications.label: How can public organisations manage challenges that cross national borders?
Which development and migration strategies work, and under what governance conditions?
How should climate change be governed across public, private and societal actors?
How does technological change affect public organisations?

alternatives.concept: Politics, international law, sociology, economics and organisational study are combined to examine how institutions and public actors respond to international social challenges. Qualitative and quantitative research support the analysis of governance and policy.
alternatives.labelRationale: The visible label was reviewed after completion of the 24-course curriculum and accurately presents this option as the closest feasible UCR response to Bachelor in Management of International Social Challenges, rather than as a narrower subfield.

alternatives.concept: Climate and sustainability questions connect governance, economics, sociology, law and communication with environmental science and technology. The programme examines both collective decisions and the physical systems involved in sustainability transitions.
basisLabels: How can public organisations manage challenges that cross national borders?
How should climate change be governed across public, private and societal actors?
alternatives.labelRationale: The visible label was reviewed after completion of the 24-course curriculum and describes its substantive organising direction without treating the generating concept as an official UCR track or overstating one strand of the programme.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces seven courses (52.5 EC) with environmental systems, sustainability governance, circular-resource study, renewable-system design, applied sustainability research and public communication. Those changes follow directly from the evidenced climate-change and Sustainable Development Goals direction.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Passed. Introduction to Sociology precedes Modern Sociology and New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory; research-method and economics courses progress from foundations to advanced work, with formal prerequisites and term availability satisfied.

courseTraceability.rationale: Law, Society & Justice provides a complementary legal foundation in administrative, constitutional and international law, legal systems and justice for analysing the institutions through which public decisions are made. It implements the explicit academic basis “Public administration and public policy” and “International law”.

Foundations of Comparative Politics Foundations of Comparative Politics provides foundational comparative-political analysis of institutions and political decision-making. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political science and multi-level governance”.

Introduction to Sociology Introduction to Sociology provides the foundational sociological concepts needed to analyse social structures and institutions. It implements the explicit academic basis “Sociology”.

Introduction to Public International Law directly studies public international law, including treaties, armed conflict, refugee law and environmental law; these are legal dimensions of cross-border social challenges. It implements the explicit academic basis “International law” and “International social and governance challenges”.

Theory of International Relations Theory of International Relations adds international-relations theory for cross-border governance and political order. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political science and multi-level governance”.

Qualitative Research Methodology directly teaches qualitative research design, data collection, analysis and dissemination through a social research project. It implements the explicit academic basis “Qualitative and quantitative social research”.

Research Methods & Statistics Research Methods & Statistics provides foundational empirical research design and statistical analysis. It implements the explicit academic basis “Qualitative and quantitative social research”.

Introduction to Economics Introduction to Economics provides foundational economic reasoning about incentives, welfare and resource allocation. It implements the explicit academic basis “Economics, welfare and economic stability”.

European Union Politics European Union Politics develops advanced understanding of European institutions and multi-level governance. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political science and multi-level governance”.

Human Rights: Law & Philosophy complements international-governance study through human-rights treaties, monitoring and case law and the historical and normative grounds of rights; it is not a public-administration methods course. It implements the explicit academic basis “International law” and “International social and governance challenges”.
Modern Sociology Modern Sociology develops modern sociological theory needed before advanced contemporary social-theory work. It implements the explicit academic basis “Sociology”.

Governance of Sustainability Governance of Sustainability directly examines sustainability policy and governance across institutional levels. It implements the explicit academic basis “International social and governance challenges”.
Public Economics Public Economics examines public-sector economics, taxation, welfare and resource allocation. It implements the explicit academic basis “Economics, welfare and economic stability”.

Peace & Conflict Peace & Conflict examines conflict, political order and governance under contested conditions. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political science and multi-level governance”.

Ethics contributes complementary normative analysis of equality, poverty, future generations, climate change and historical injustice, supporting the evidenced distinction between normative judgments and empirical governance analysis. It implements the explicit academic basis “International social and governance challenges”.

International Macroeconomics International Macroeconomics adds macroeconomic analysis of international economic conditions and policy. It implements the explicit academic basis “Economics, welfare and economic stability”.

Psychology of Organizations & Leadership Psychology of Organizations & Leadership provides organisational-psychology theory on motivation, leadership, groups and organisational culture. It implements the explicit academic basis “Organisation and management”.

New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory adds advanced analysis of contemporary social theory, civil society and institutional change. It implements the explicit academic basis “Sociology”.

Climate Change directly examines a named MISOC challenge through climate drivers and impacts, adaptation, mitigation, justice and governance; scientific and social aspects are distinguished. It implements the explicit academic basis “International social and governance challenges”.

Foundations of European Union Law directly examines EU institutions, legal foundations, citizenship and free movement, enabling legal analysis of European governance alongside political study. It implements the explicit academic basis “Global and European governance” and “International law”.

Econometrics directly teaches quantitative causal and predictive analysis using regression, instrumental variables, statistical tests and an empirical economic paper. It implements the explicit academic basis “Qualitative and quantitative social research” and “Economics, welfare and economic stability”.

Leadership & Diversity Management Leadership & Diversity Management examines leadership and diversity in organisational settings. It implements the explicit academic basis “Organisation and management”.

Social Movements & Environmental Justice examines social movements and environmental justice using environmental-conflict cases, contributing directly to the social mobilisation and inequality dimensions of international sustainability challenges. It implements the explicit academic basis “International social and governance challenges”.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Formal prerequisites and all six planned terms checked directly against the enriched workbook. Climate Change precedes Governance of Sustainability; the latter has no formal prerequisite and introduces governance concepts, so semester-2 placement is defensible. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and the dependent 300-level technical courses; Introduction to Sociology precedes Modern Sociology and contemporary social theory. Early 300-level status alone is not a progression defect.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match and the climate/sustainability governance route are both defensible. The climate route is the strongest additional option because its evidence produces a genuine seven-course curricular shift. A migration/development candidate could not support a third alternative: the substitutions needed to cross the threshold did not implement migration or development and therefore failed qualitative distinctness. The technology-and-public-organisations interest was also assessed for completeness and found not feasible as a coherent 24-course route.

notes.text: The Erasmus programme combines a structured Public Administration curriculum with international law, migration, development, research methods and a bachelor project. UCR can assemble strong multidisciplinary programmes around global governance and specific international challenges, but does not reproduce the same dedicated MISOC sequence or its named International Migration and Global Development Issues courses.

audience.programmeDescription: Management of International Social Challenges at Erasmus University Rotterdam examines how public organisations address problems across national borders, including migration, global development, climate change and economic instability. Students study politics, policy, international law, sociology, economics and management alongside social research and a bachelor project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines substantial governance, international law, political, social, economic, organisational and research study. A second option focuses on climate and sustainability governance, including complementary environmental science and technology. These are related UCR programmes rather than equivalents to Erasmus’s dedicated MISOC curriculum; the specialist migration and development courses, policy-analysis sequence and required 15-EC bachelor project remain gaps.
